The air in the atrium hummed with a nervous energy June recognized well. It wasn't the electric buzz of anticipation for the demonstration itself – that would come later, with the throng of journalists and curious onlookers. This was the quiet, frantic thrum of a man wrestling with perfection, with the infinitesimal details that could make or break a public showing. And that man, Dr. Alistair Finch, was currently wrestling with a recalcitrant power cable.

June navigated the maze of equipment with practiced ease, dodging a stray laser pointer beam and sidestepping a precariously balanced stack of data pads. Alistair's lab, typically a controlled chaos of wires and schematics, had been transplanted wholesale into the grand, echoing space of the city's Innovation Hub. It looked, she thought, like a particularly ambitious science fair project had exploded. 

“Still battling the grid, I see?” she offered, her voice calm amidst the controlled chaos. She knelt beside him, her eyes quickly assessing the problem. A frayed connection, easily remedied. She pulled a small toolkit from her bag, the familiar weight grounding her.

Alistair, a man perpetually on the verge of dishevelment with a shock of white hair defying gravity, didn't look up. "The city's power is… temperamental today," he muttered, more to the cable than to her. "It needs to be flawless, June. Absolutely flawless." 

June, having secured the connection with a practiced twist of a screwdriver, straightened up. "It will be. You've run countless simulations. The core algorithms are locked. We've got this." She offered him a small, reassuring smile. Alistair, for all his brilliance, tended to get lost in the weeds of technical details, forgetting the bigger picture. That’s where she came in. She was the pragmatist, the organizer, the calm eye in his storm of invention. 

The demonstration was meant to be simple. A live demonstration of the ‘Chrono-Weave,’ a device Alistair claimed could analyze and extrapolate temporal patterns – essentially, predict probabilities with unprecedented accuracy. He’d framed it as a tool for urban planning, resource management, even preventative medicine. A way to smooth out the jagged edges of the future. 

She glanced at the polished chrome sphere that was the heart of the Chrono-Weave. It pulsed with a soft, internal light, a mesmerizing dance of blues and greens. It looked, she had to admit, breathtaking. And if Alistair's claims were true… the implications were staggering. The crowd was expected in less than an hour.
